findings.title: Room rent above your policy limit
findings.explanation_en: Your policy allows 5,000/day; the room was billed at 7,500/day for 1 day(s).

explanations.en: Your policy allows 5,000/day; the room was billed at 7,500/day for 1 day(s).

findings.fix: No fix can remove this before submission. You stayed 1 day in Deluxe room billed at Rs 7,500/day vs eligible Rs 5,000/day under Clause 3.1. Patient bears Rs 2,500 excess. For next admission, tell admission desk: 'Please allot only my eligible room category up to Rs 5,000/day as per policy and give it in writing' and keep that allotment slip.

policy_cite.quote: Room rent, boarding and nursing expenses are payable up to 1% of the Sum Insured per day.

cite.quote: Room rent, boarding and nursing expenses are payable up to 1% of the Sum Insured per day.

tool_evidence.tpa_reasoning: 1 day Deluxe room charged exceeds 1% SI eligible limit per evidence pack room analysis; excess is non-payable and triggers proportionate deduction. Policy continuous 80 months so no waiting defence.
tool_evidence.advocate_argument: Clause 3.1 limits room rent to 1% SI = Rs 5,000/day. Charged Rs 7,500 x 1 day = Rs 7,500. Excess Rs 2,500 is correctly non-payable. Ratio 5000/7500=0.6666 is correct and triggers Clause 3.3.

findings.title: Proportionate deduction on doctor/OT/nursing fees
findings.explanation_en: Because the room exceeded the limit, the insurer scales associated charges (32,700) by 67%, cutting 10,900. Pharmacy, consumables, implants and diagnostics (22,500) are protected from this cut.

explanations.en: Because the room exceeded the limit, the insurer scales associated charges (32,700) by 67%, cutting 10,900. Pharmacy, consumables, implants and diagnostics (22,500) are protected from this cut.

findings.fix: Ask Hospital Billing Desk / Medical Superintendent BEFORE submission for a certificate on letterhead with seal, sign, IP number and dates stating: 'Certified that doctor, OT, nursing charges for items L02-L05 are uniform and we do not do differential billing by room category for this admission.' Upload it with the final itemized bill. If hospital confirms they charge same for all rooms, Rs 10,900 proportionate cut goes away. If they refuse because they do charge higher for Deluxe, the cut stays.

policy_cite.quote: If the insured person is admitted in a room category with rent higher than the eligible limit, the associated medical expenses shall be payable in the same proportion as the eligible room rent bears to the actual room rent, except for pharmacy, consumables, implants, medical devices and diagnostics.

cite.quote: If the insured person is admitted in a room category with rent higher than the eligible limit, the associated medical expenses shall be payable in the same proportion as the eligible room rent bears to the actual room rent, except for pharmacy, consumables, implants, medical devices and diagnostics.

tool_evidence.tpa_reasoning: Room rent exceeds eligible limit, so associated medical expenses L02, L03, L04, L05 are payable only in eligible-to-charged ratio per clause 3.3. Exempt categories correctly excluded: implant L06, pharmacy L07, investigations L08. No miscategorisation requiring recategorize_item.
tool_evidence.advocate_argument: If PD applies, calculation is correct per Clause 3.3: associated total Rs 32,700 x (1-0.6666) = Rs 10,900, with pharmacy/implant/investigations Rs 22,500 correctly exempted (L06,L07,L08). But PD applies only where hospital actually bills differentially by room. With a no-differential-billing certificate the Rs 10,900 can be removed pre-submission.
